p.i: min adjectivo postpositum, sequente sub-stantivo, ut supra in litera ם Mem dic-tum est.
Quae viro, aut rebus viri specie con-ceptis congruunt, ut דָּיִד[?] David: אָב ab, pater: כָּרַת[?] Peráth, fluvius Euphrates.
Deinde omne Adjectivum est masculi-ni generis, & movetur in foemininum, assumpta litera ה, quam semper praecedit ־ camez, ut, טוֹב tob, bonus, טוֹבָה tobah bona.

Adjectivum participiale movetur in foemininum, assumpta litera ה He, quam praecedit ־ camez, vel (in regimine) af-sumpta litera ת tau, quam praecedit ֽ se-gol, ut, פּוֹקֵד pokéd, vir visitas, פּוֹקְדָה vel פּוֹקֵדֶת pokedáh vel pokédeth, foemina visitans.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points on דָּיִד, כָּרַת and the Hebrew words of the last paragraph are read from a small scan; the pointing is doubtful and marked where uncertain. The question lines are set in roman type, the answers and the body in italic. The Hebrew letter ת in the segol rule is printed as shown.
